messages:
Jordan K: quick thread on private endpoint certs + control-plane dependency. current operator-copy approach is high-friction for onboarding and painful during rotations. thoughts on alternatives?
Priya S: agreed. main goals: (1) no long-lived file copies, (2) auditable issuance, (3) resilient if CP <-> tenant peering flakes.
Liam O: proposal A: ephemeral certs via a CP signing API reachable over PrivateLink/peering. agent requests a short-lived cert on CSR, CP signs and returns. we keep logs and revoke centrally.
Nadia V: sounds similar to earlier ideas, but we need explicit fallback semantics. what happens during regional CP outage? agents should not become bricked.
Jordan K: fallback options brainstormed: a) agent uses a locally cached cert until expiry (with short TTL), b) operator pre-seeds a time-limited offline cert during onboarding, c) local offline signer shim (customer-run) that can sign CSRs using a key injected during install.
Priya S: tradeoffs: (a) reduces availability risk but increases window for compromised certs if agent stolen. (b) keeps operator involvement but is still a file copy. (c) ok for air-gapped installs but increases support surface.
Liam O: operational model I'd prefer: primary = CP signing API; fallback chain = cached cert -> offline pre-seed -> read-only mode. add a diagnostic metric that shows percentage of agents on fallback.
Nadia V: auth model: issue short token from CP token-server over peering (OAuth-style), then agent calls signing API with CSR+token. tokens are scoped to install id and single-use or short TTL (60s-5m). tokens let us log requester identity without sharing CA private keys.
Jordan K: revoke story: maintain a per-install revocation list exposed to agents (pull model) and also push via control channel to agents when we revoke urgent certificates. in network partition, agents must check local revocation cache.
Priya S: choose certificate lifetime carefully. recommendation: 12h default, 1h for high-security tenants. shorter lifetimes force more churn but reduce compromise blast radius. also need to rate-limit signing requests to prevent abuse.
Liam O: network topology note: some customers SNAT through a shared IP. signing API must accept tenant identity in token; don't rely on src ip. also consider splitting signing API regionally so cross-region peering doesn't add latency.
Nadia V: security: all agent <> signing API calls must be mTLS mutual auth plus token. Keys for mTLS are from previous certs; bootstrap flow needs special-case. we can use a short-lived bootstrap cert issued by operator during install or a pre-shared install token exchanged at setup time.
Jordan K: bootstrap options: - operator-copy (legacy) - install-time interactive CSR with human-in-the-loop - preseeded bootstrap identity stored in customer CP (for private deployments)
Priya S: logging & audit: every issuance should write an immutable record (w/ requestor id, install id, signing CA id, CSR fingerprint, TTL). store in WORM storage and surface in Console.
Liam O: alerts: signing API error rate > 1% or latency p95 > 500ms -> page oncall. also a daily report of fallback usage per-region/tenant.
Nadia V: deploy and rollout: feature flag per-tenant. start by offering signing API for new tenants only, keep operator-copy for legacy until migration tooling exists.
Jordan K: migration plan: a migration tool will rotate to ephemeral certs by issuing an initial bootstrap token and rotating any preseeded keys. need a dry-run mode and a rollback plan.
Priya S: edge-case: what if CP signs leafs but root rotation needs coordination w/ customer CA? offer an interoperable mode where CP signs with an intermediate that chains to customer root (requires proving control).
Liam O: final callouts: - ensure revocation cache TTL and update frequency tuned for typical partition windows - document offline shim pattern for air-gapped installs - add SLOs & runbook for signing API outages
DeployBot: reminder: schedule staging canary for signing-api tomorrow 2026-03-26 02:00 UTC. command: ```infra deploy canary --service signing-api --env staging --tag canary-ephemeral-cert```
Jordan K: I'll write an RFC addendum capturing the signing API flow, bootstrap modes, fallback chain, and migration plan. assigning follow-ups: @Liam O prototyping regional signer + token server, @Nadia V threat model and bootstrap options, @Priya S Console audit surface + metrics. aiming RFC patch by EOW. thanks all.
